title: Valid and invalid competitor names
objective: Agree which competitor names are valid, then verify how the app handles empty, duplicate, very long and special-character names.
steps: Agree with the product owner which names are valid and what the app must say for an invalid one.
In a TP- competition, try an empty name, a name that already exists, a 200-character name and a name with a comma and a quote.
Check the message for each and that invalid names are not added, also after a page reload.
expected_result: Invalid names are rejected with a clear message and are not added; valid names are added.
reason_manual: Needs a product decision on what a valid name is before it can be automated.

title: Valid and invalid result values
objective: Agree limits and messages for invalid result values and verify them per event.
steps: Agree with the product owner the valid range per event and the expected message.
In a TP- competition, try an empty, a negative, a non-numeric and a very large value for one time event and one distance event.
Check the message and that no invalid value is saved, also after a page reload.
expected_result: Invalid values are rejected with a clear message and are not saved.
reason_manual: Needs a product decision on the limits before it can be automated.

title: Replace an existing result
objective: Verify what happens when a result is saved for an event that already has one.
steps: In a TP- competition, save a valid result for a competitor and an event.
Save a different valid result for the same competitor and event.
Answer the confirmation dialog once with 'No, keep it' and once with 'Yes, replace', and check the standings each time.
expected_result: 'No' keeps the old result and its points; 'Yes' replaces them; the standings and total follow the choice.
reason_manual: The requirement gives no criterion for replacing a result; a person should agree the expected behaviour first.

title: Edit and remove a competitor
objective: Verify editing a competitor's name and results, and removing a competitor.
steps: In a TP- competition, click a competitor row to open the edit dialog.
Change the name and a result and save; then open it again and remove the competitor.
Check the standings and total after each change.
expected_result: Changes are shown in the standings and are kept after a reload; a removed competitor is no longer listed.
reason_manual: Editing and removing data was outside the scope and no criterion exists; run by a person on disposable data.

title: Points and ranking per event
objective: Compare the points and the ranking with the official combined-events scoring tables.
steps: Agree the scoring tables that apply (World Athletics, current version).
In a TP- competition, enter reference results for every Decathlon event for two competitors.
Compare each event's points and the total with the tables, and check the order of the standings.
expected_result: Points per event and total equal the tables; positions follow the totals.
reason_manual: Needs the scoring tables as a reference before it can be automated.

title: CSV export matches the table
objective: Verify that the exported CSV contains the same data as the standings.
steps: In a TP- competition with results, click 'Export CSV' on the Decathlon tab.
Open the file and compare every competitor, total, position and event value with the table.
Repeat with a name that contains a comma.
expected_result: The CSV has every competitor and value shown in the table, and names with a comma stay intact.
reason_manual: The export was not in scope and gives a download that a person should inspect.

title: Page width at 375 px
objective: Decide whether the page may be wider than a 375 px screen and check the layout on a real phone.
steps: Open http://localhost:8080 at 375x812 (or a real phone) and select a TP- competition with competitors.
Check whether the page scrolls sideways and whether the standings table can be read and reached.
Agree the expected behaviour (for example a table that scrolls inside its own box).
expected_result: The page does not scroll sideways, or the table scrolls in its own box, as agreed.
reason_manual: No requirement gives a layout criterion and there is no design reference; a person must decide what is acceptable.

title: Long Jump result after a reload
objective: Verify that a saved Long Jump result is still there after a page reload.
steps: In a TP- competition, save a Long Jump result for a competitor (in cm).
Reload the page and select the competition.
Check that the Long Jump result and its points are still shown.
expected_result: The Long Jump result and its points are still shown after the reload.
reason_manual: Can be automated; proposed as a follow-up to TPI-008, which did not reload after saving.
